title: Greetings & Names (问候与名字)
description: Say hello at different times of day, ask how people are, introduce yourself, ask someone's name, and use Chinese name order and polite titles.

notes.heading: 📌 Core Greetings
notes.body:
The most famous Chinese word is 你好 **nǐ hǎo** — literally 'you good'. It works any time of day. To be extra polite (to teachers or adults), say 您好 **nín hǎo** with the respectful form of 'you'.

Match your greeting to the time of day:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 你好 | nǐ hǎo | hello |
| 您好 | nín hǎo | hello (polite) |
| 早上好 | zǎoshang hǎo | good morning |
| 下午好 | xiàwǔ hǎo | good afternoon |
| 晚上好 | wǎnshang hǎo | good evening |
| 再见 | zàijiàn | goodbye |

💡 **Worked Example:** 再见 zàijiàn literally means 'again see' — like 'see you again'. Use it when leaving, to anyone: 老师再见！(Goodbye, teacher!)

notes.heading: ❓ Asking 'How Are You?' — 你好吗？
notes.body:
**你好吗？Nǐ hǎo ma?** means 'How are you?' The little word 吗 **ma** is a question particle: put it at the end of any statement and it becomes a yes/no question. 你好 (you are well) + 吗 = 你好吗？(are you well?).

Typical answers:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 我很好。 | Wǒ hěn hǎo. | I'm very well. |
| 很好，谢谢。 | Hěn hǎo, xièxie. | Very well, thanks. |
| 你呢？ | Nǐ ne? | And you? |
| 我也很好。 | Wǒ yě hěn hǎo. | I'm very well too. |

🔑 **How it works:** 很 **hěn** means 'very', but in sentences like 我很好 it often just links the subject to the adjective and does not always mean 'very' strongly. 也 **yě** means 'also/too'.

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** don't answer 你好吗 with just 好 — the natural full answer is 我很好 or 很好，谢谢.

notes.heading: 🙋 Introducing Yourself — 我叫 and 我是
notes.body:
Two easy patterns tell people who you are:

- **我叫 … Wǒ jiào …** — 'I am called …' (my name is)
- **我是 … Wǒ shì …** — 'I am …'

💡 **Worked Example:**
- 我叫小明。Wǒ jiào Xiǎomíng. — My name is Xiaoming.
- 我是小红。Wǒ shì Xiǎohóng. — I am Xiaohong.

You can chain them with a greeting:
你好！我叫小明。Nǐ hǎo! Wǒ jiào Xiǎomíng. — Hello! My name is Xiaoming.

📎 **Key Points:**
- 叫 **jiào** = to be called; 是 **shì** = to be (am/is/are).
- 我 **wǒ** = I/me; 你 **nǐ** = you.
- Chinese verbs never change form — 是 stays 是 for I, you, he, she, we.

notes.heading: 🏷️ Chinese Name Order: Surname First
notes.body:
Chinese names put the **surname (姓 xìng) first** and the **given name (名字 míngzi) after** — the opposite of English order.

💡 **Worked Example:** in the name 王小明 **Wáng Xiǎomíng**, 王 is the surname and 小明 is the given name. In English order this would be Xiaoming Wang.

Common Chinese surnames:

| Character | Pinyin |
|---|---|
| 王 | Wáng |
| 李 | Lǐ |
| 张 | Zhāng |
| 刘 | Liú |
| 陈 | Chén |

📎 **Key Points:**
- Most surnames are one character; given names are usually one or two characters.
- Family comes first in Chinese culture — the name order reflects this.
- To say your surname: 我姓王。Wǒ xìng Wáng. — My surname is Wang.

notes.heading: 🎩 Titles: 老师, 先生, 女士
notes.body:
Titles go **after the surname** in Chinese:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 老师 | lǎoshī | teacher |
| 先生 | xiānsheng | Mr / sir |
| 女士 | nǚshì | Ms / madam |
| 小姐 | xiǎojiě | Miss / young lady |

💡 **Worked Example:**
- 王老师 Wáng lǎoshī — Teacher Wang
- 李先生 Lǐ xiānsheng — Mr Li
- 张老师好！Zhāng lǎoshī hǎo! — Hello, Teacher Zhang!

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** English says 'Mr Li' (title first), but Chinese says 李先生 (surname first, title after). Never say 先生李.

📎 **Key Point:** calling a teacher 老师 directly (王老师好) is polite and normal — you do not need to say 先生 to a teacher.

notes.heading: 🗣️ Asking Someone's Name
notes.body:
Two key questions:

- **你叫什么名字？Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?** — What is your name? (literally: you called what name?)
- **你姓什么？Nǐ xìng shénme?** — What is your surname?

Answers:
- 我叫小红。Wǒ jiào Xiǎohóng. — My name is Xiaohong.
- 我姓王。Wǒ xìng Wáng. — My surname is Wang.

To be very polite when asking an adult's surname, say **您贵姓？Nín guìxìng?** — 'What is your honourable surname?'

🔑 **How it works:** 什么 **shénme** means 'what'. Chinese questions keep the normal word order — the question word simply replaces the thing you are asking about: 你叫**什么**名字？

notes.heading: 🏫 Classroom Language & Polite Words
notes.body:
Everyday words you will hear in a Chinese classroom:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 上课 | shàngkè | class begins |
| 下课 | xiàkè | class is over |
| 请 | qǐng | please |
| 请坐 | qǐng zuò | please sit down |
| 谢谢 | xièxie | thank you |
| 不客气 | bú kèqi | you're welcome |
| 对不起 | duìbuqǐ | sorry |
| 没关系 | méi guānxi | it doesn't matter / that's OK |
| 听 / 说 / 读 / 写 | tīng / shuō / dú / xiě | listen / speak / read / write |

💡 **Worked Example:**
A: 谢谢老师！Xièxie lǎoshī! — Thank you, teacher!
B: 不客气！Bú kèqi! — You're welcome!

📎 **Key Points:**
- Answer 对不起 (sorry) with 没关系 (that's OK).
- Answer 谢谢 (thanks) with 不客气 (you're welcome).
- These polite pairs are used constantly — learn them as fixed chunks.

flashcards.example: 你好，我叫小明。Nǐ hǎo, wǒ jiào Xiǎomíng. (Hello, my name is Xiaoming.)

flashcards.definition: How are you? — 吗 turns the statement 你好 into a question.
flashcards.example: 你好吗？我很好。Nǐ hǎo ma? Wǒ hěn hǎo. (How are you? I'm very well.)

flashcards.definition: I'm very well — the standard reply to 你好吗.
flashcards.example: 我很好，谢谢。Wǒ hěn hǎo, xièxie. (I'm very well, thank you.)

flashcards.definition: To be called — used to give your name: 我叫… (my name is…).
flashcards.example: 我叫小红。Wǒ jiào Xiǎohóng. (My name is Xiaohong.)
我是学生。Wǒ shì xuésheng. (I am a student.)

flashcards.definition: Surname; also the verb 'to be surnamed'.
flashcards.example: 我姓王。Wǒ xìng Wáng. (My surname is Wang.)
你叫什么名字？Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi? (What is your name?)

flashcards.definition: Teacher — goes after the surname: 王老师 (Teacher Wang).
flashcards.example: 王老师好！Wáng lǎoshī hǎo! (Hello, Teacher Wang!)

flashcards.definition: Mr / sir — goes after the surname: 李先生 (Mr Li).
flashcards.example: 李先生是老师。Lǐ xiānsheng shì lǎoshī. (Mr Li is a teacher.)

flashcards.definition: Thank you. The reply is 不客气 (you're welcome).
Sorry. The reply is 没关系 (that's OK).
flashcards.example: 对不起，我迟到了。Duìbuqǐ, wǒ chídào le. (Sorry, I'm late.)

questions.explanation: 你好 literally means 'you good' and is the standard Chinese greeting, usable at any time of day.
再见 zàijiàn literally means 'see you again' and is the everyday way to say goodbye.
老师 lǎoshī means teacher. It is also a polite title used after the surname, as in 王老师 (Teacher Wang).

questions.stem: Which sentence asks 'What is your name?'
choices: 你叫什么名字？Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?
questions.explanation: 你叫什么名字？literally asks 'you are called what name?' — 什么 (shénme) means 'what' and 名字 (míngzi) means 'name'.

questions.stem: 我叫小明。(Wǒ jiào Xiǎomíng.) means:
questions.explanation: 我叫 … is the standard self-introduction pattern: 我 (I) + 叫 (am called) + name.

questions.stem: In the Chinese name 王小红 (Wáng Xiǎohóng), which part is the surname?
questions.explanation: Chinese names put the surname first, so 王 (Wáng) is the surname and 小红 (Xiǎohóng) is the given name — the opposite of English name order.

questions.stem: Someone greets you with 你好吗？(Nǐ hǎo ma?) What is the natural reply?
choices: 我很好，谢谢。Wǒ hěn hǎo, xièxie.
你叫什么名字？Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?
questions.explanation: 我很好，谢谢 ('I'm very well, thanks') is the standard answer to 你好吗. You can then ask back with 你呢？(And you?).

questions.stem: What does the word 吗 (ma) do in 你好吗？
choices: It turns a statement into a yes/no question
questions.explanation: 吗 is a question particle: adding it to the end of the statement 你好 (you are well) creates the question 你好吗 (are you well?).

questions.stem: You meet your Chinese teacher, an adult you respect. Which greeting is most polite?
questions.explanation: 您 nín is the polite, respectful form of 你, so 您好 is the most respectful hello — ideal for teachers and adults. 喂 is only used when answering the phone.

questions.stem: 你呢？(Nǐ ne?) is used to mean:
questions.explanation: 呢 (ne) bounces the previous question back: after answering 我很好, you ask 你呢？— 'I'm well, and you?'
谢谢 xièxie means thank you. The polite reply is 不客气 (bú kèqi) — you're welcome.

questions.stem: Which is the correct Chinese way to say 'Mr Zhang'?
questions.explanation: In Chinese the surname comes first and the title follows: 张先生 = Mr Zhang. English order (title first) is a common learner mistake.

questions.stem: An adult politely asks you 您贵姓？(Nín guìxìng?) What is the correct reply?
choices: 我姓李。Wǒ xìng Lǐ. — My surname is Li.
我叫李。Wǒ jiào Lǐ. — I am called Li.
我很好。Wǒ hěn hǎo. — I'm very well.
questions.explanation: 贵姓 asks for your surname, so the answer uses 我姓 … (my surname is …). 我叫 … gives your full or given name, not the answer to this question.

questions.stem: The teacher says 上课！(shàngkè) at the start of the lesson. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 上课 shàngkè announces that class is beginning; its opposite is 下课 xiàkè — class is over.

questions.stem: 不客气 (bú kèqi) is the polite reply to:
questions.explanation: 不客气 literally means 'don't be polite' and is the standard reply to 谢谢, just like 'you're welcome' in English.
